topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the multistep mutation model, and the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase signaling promote sustained cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells evade terminal differentiation in hematological malignancies and intestinal epithelial renewal.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death by altering the p53 pathway and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Telomere dynamics, cellular senescence, and growth-control summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by overcoming telomere shortening and senescence, concluding with a summary of growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells alter their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific rewiring, and metabolic gene mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch, the balance of angiogenic activators and inhibitors, and the necessity of vascularization for tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dynamics, and genomics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metastatic cascade, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and genomic findings including whole genome duplication in metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks, recommended reading on cancer hallmarks, and practical session housekeeping.
